explanation: The N88S mutation reduces atazanavir binding through loss of a critical hydrogen-bonding network rather than direct ligand contact. Asparagine at position 88 likely forms a stabilizing hydrogen bond (either through its amide side chain or backbone interactions) that maintains the precise geometry of the C-terminal dimer interface; substitution with serine's smaller hydroxyl group weakens or eliminates this interaction, destabilizing the protease dimer architecture. This local conformational perturbation propagates ~7–15 Å to the active site, subtly distorting the inhibitor binding pocket and weakening atazanavir binding through cumulative loss of complementary van der Waals contacts and hydrogen bond geometry rather than introducing steric clash.
